name: Rimehart
description: A dun horse out of the snow forests with a rack of antlers on mare and stallion alike, swept back and over with a tine thrown forward above the face. No two racks match, and no rack matches itself: the two sides grow differently, as a reindeer's do. Some carry moss on the tines, and a few have points that glow through the polar night. Stocky, shaggy and untroubled by any cold.
notes: ANTLERS ON BOTH SEXES. Every founder carries Ant, the allele that grows antlers on a mare as well as a stallion - the reindeer's arrangement, and the reason this breed exists. One in five also carries Antm, the stallion-only allele, silently: Ant is dominant over it, so it only surfaces when two Rimeharts each pass it on, and then it is the mares of that line that go bare.

BROW-TINED. 70 in 100 are Brw/Brw; 15 carry Frk under it and show brow-tined anyway, and 15 carry Pal over it and show palmate - Pal is the top of the antler_form series. A palmate Rimehart bred to a plain one throws half brow-tined foals.

ASYMMETRIC, AND THE FIRST BREED TO PIN IT. No wild horse has any asymmetry - every founder rolls exactly zero and drift cannot move it (decision D3) - so the only way to a lopsided rack is a breed that writes the value. This one bands it 0.15 to 0.45: past 0.1 the left antler grows a different rack from the right, and the more of it a horse has, the fewer tines and the shorter beam on that side. Bred to an unrelated antlered horse, the foals' copies carry the number on, so a line keeps its lopsidedness without the breed.

SIZE AND TINES ARE BANDED UP. A wild antlered horse is drawn from the lower part of the size ladder with one to six tines; a Rimehart sits from small to large with three and a half to six and a half. Neither is a ceiling: a line bred for size climbs to a massive rack, and the clamp stops it there.
Moss, not leaves: every Rimehart that blooms grows moss (growth index 1). A fifth carry the bloom silently. A few have glowing points, and another fifth carry them.

Dun over bay or black - bay dun and grullo - with pangare paling the muzzle and belly, so the coat reads grey-brown with a light underside, the reindeer's colours. Cold-tolerant (Ctol/Ctol) like every snow breed.
